name: @olai/sigterm
//main: The guard IS the module: installSigtermGuard is the only call the composition root makes, and judge/SI/who are the pure policy it owes tests. @olai/server's main.ts installs it at boot; nothing else imports it — that one edge is the whole dependency surface of a mechanism that can exit the process.
//dependencies: None, on purpose. The mechanism is the runtime's own FFI over libc (compiled at boot with the runtime's embedded compiler — see src/sigterm.ts's WHY-NATIVE) and node's built-ins; a package whose job is to say no to signals should carry no import whose resolution could fail first.
//own-c: src/sigterm.c must sit ON DISK beside src/sigterm.ts at runtime: the guard joins import.meta.dir and hands the runtime's embedded compiler a filesystem path (a few lines of freestanding C, never linked, compiled in-process at boot). True today because the server ships and runs as raw TypeScript from the store; a future bundling step that inlined the module would meet 'guard unavailable' at boot rather than at build. Production is Linux/NixOS only; on darwin the file is data and the entry point returns early.
